subject: general
question: In which year was the East India Company granted 'Diwani rights' (right to collect revenues and decide civil cases of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa) by Mughals?
solution:
The correct answer is **__1765__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The East India Company acquired the Diwani rights over Bengal in the year 1765.
 
• This marked a pivotal turning point in Indian history, as it effectively established British control over the region's administration and finances.
 
• The Diwani, or the right to collect land revenue, was a crucial source of income for the Mughal Empire, and its transfer to the Company signified a significant erosion of Mughal authority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The acquisition of the Diwani rights stemmed from the Battle of Buxar,
 
• It was fought on October 23, 1764, between the British East India Company forces led by Robert Clive and the combined armies of Mir Qasim (the Nawab of Bengal), Shuja-ud-Daulah (the Nawab of Awadh), and the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II.
 
• The battle resulted in a decisive British victory, paving the way for the Company to secure the Diwani rights through the Treaty of Allahabad signed on August 12, 1765.
 
• Under the terms of the treaty, Shah Alam II granted the East India Company the Diwani rights in return for an annual tribute of 26 lakhs of rupees.
 
• This grant of power allowed the Company to directly collect taxes from the people of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa, significantly bolstering its financial resources and solidifying its dominance in the region.Under the terms of the treaty, Shah Alam II granted the East India Company the Diwani rights in return for an annual tribute of 26 lakhs of rupees.
